study.title: Auxiliary Input in Training: Incorporating Catheter Features into Deep Learning Models for ECG-Free Dynamic Coronary Roadmapping
study.venue: International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention (MICCAI)

imaging.modality_detail: Non-subtracted X-ray coronary angiography sequences paired with contrast-free X-ray fluoroscopy streams; frame rates 7.5, 15 or 30 fps; image sizes 492x492 to 624x624 after normalizing pixel spacing to 0.2 mm
imaging.territory_detail: Coronary arteries (dynamic coronary roadmapping for PCI)

public_dataset_used.detail: All experiments used in-house data (CPM: 2483 angiography-fluoroscopy video pairs, 174228 frames; CTT: 4098 videos, 255432 frames)

task.task_description: Auxiliary Input in Training (AIT): catheter masks appended as an extra input channel and progressively ablated during training, applied to ECG-free cardiac phase matching between angiographic and live fluoroscopic sequences and to guiding-catheter tip tracking.
task.clinical_application: ECG-free dynamic coronary roadmapping for navigation during percutaneous coronary interventions, reducing contrast and radiation

temporal_evidence.quote: a temporal neural network to infer temporal relations between image features, for which we experimented with both ConvLSTM and Transformer backbones

method.explainability_method: Feature map visualization using first three principal components as RGB channels
